x: They cover seven districts (4 Rayalaseema + 3 North Coastal); new units there get 15% additional depreciation and 15% investment allowance.

s: Under Section 94, what additional depreciation do new industrial units in the backward districts get?
x: New units get 15% additional depreciation and a 15% investment allowance.

s: Which sub-section of Section 94 of the AP Reorganisation Act provides for tax incentives?
x: Section 94(1) covers fiscal measures including tax incentives; 94(2) covers backward-area infrastructure.

s: Which company's unit near Tirupati is part of rebuilding Rayalaseema as an industrial hub?
x: Rayalaseema's industrial-hub development is associated with Kia, JSW, Royal Enfield near Tirupati and the Space City.

s: Sri City, a multi-product SEZ, lies in which district?
x: Sri City is a multi-product SEZ in Tirupati district.

s: Which period does Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Development Policy 4.0 cover?
x: Industrial Development Policy 4.0 covers 2024-29.

s: How many BHAVYA industrial parks were proposed in Andhra Pradesh in August 2026?
x: Six BHAVYA parks were proposed in August 2026 under the Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29).

s: Why did the retention of corporate and bank regional headquarters in Hyderabad create a difficulty for residual Andhra Pradesh?
o: It deprived the State of all banking services
It prevented the formation of any district administration
It left the State without a commercial nerve centre
It transferred all ports to Telangana
x: Corporate and bank regional headquarters stayed in Hyderabad, leaving residual Andhra Pradesh without a commercial nerve centre.

s: Which of the following was NOT a cause of the investment slowdown in Andhra Pradesh after 2014?
x: The slowdown came from capital uncertainty, no ready administrative set-up and agitations; AP has a long coastline.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank in the 2015 BRAP ease of doing business ranking?
x: In 2015 AP ranked 2nd, behind Gujarat.

s: In BRAP 2019, which State ranked first?
x: AP ranked first in BRAP 2019, with UP second and Telangana third.

s: Which State ranked first in the Asia Competitiveness Institute's 2019 ease of doing business ranking?
x: In the Asia Competitiveness Institute's 2019 ranking, Andhra Pradesh was 1st, followed by Maharashtra and Delhi.

s: In the 2016 BRAP ease of doing business ranking, with which State did Andhra Pradesh share the first rank?
x: In BRAP 2016 Andhra Pradesh and Telangana were joint first; in 2015 AP was second after Gujarat.

s: What is the correct expansion of APEPDCL?
o: Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited
Andhra Pradesh Energy Power Development Company Limited
Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Corporation Limited
Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Development Corporation Limited
x: APEPDCL stands for Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited.

s: In which year was the present Vijayawada-based APCPDCL carved out of APSPDCL?
x: The new APCPDCL was carved out of APSPDCL in 2020; the pre-2014 APCPDCL was headquartered at Hyderabad.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its old-district jurisdiction?
o: APSPDCL — Nellore, Chittoor, Kadapa, Anantapur and Kurnool
x: Krishna, Guntur and Prakasam were associated with APCPDCL. APEPDCL covered Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and the two Godavari districts.

s: Which of the following was NOT one of the four DISCOMs formed in the 2000 unbundling?
x: The 2000 arrangement had EPDCL-Visakhapatnam, CPDCL-Hyderabad, NPDCL-Warangal and SPDCL-Tirupati; the Vijayawada-based APCPDCL was formed later.

s: Which scheme, introduced in 2021, replaced UDAY in power distribution reform?
x: The Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), introduced in 2021, replaced UDAY (2015).

s: In which year was UDAY (Ujwal Discom Assurance Yojana) approved?
x: UDAY was approved in November 2015; it was replaced by RDSS in 2021.

s: What is the full form of APCPDCL?
o: Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Company Limited
Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Corporation Limited
Andhra Pradesh Central Power Development Corporation Limited
Andhra Pradesh Coastal Power Distribution Company Limited
x: APCPDCL is the Central Power Distribution Corporation Ltd; the other two DISCOMs (APEPDCL, APSPDCL) are 'Company' Ltd.

s: Where is the headquarters of APSPDCL (AP Southern Power Distribution Company Ltd)?
x: APSPDCL is headquartered at Tirupati; APEPDCL is at Visakhapatnam and APCPDCL at Vijayawada.

s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, which two districts were moved to APSPDCL?
x: After bifurcation, Anantapur and Kurnool (earlier under CPDCL Hyderabad) were moved to APSPDCL.

s: Which of the following sources has no share in Andhra Pradesh's installed power capacity?
x: AP's capacity mix is thermal, hydel, gas and renewables; it has no nuclear capacity.

s: For how many hours do Andhra Pradesh's 22.36 lakh farm pump sets receive free daytime power?
x: The 22.36 lakh farm pump sets get nine hours of free daytime power; aqua power is priced at Rs 1.50 per unit.

s: Which renewable-energy source has the largest installed capacity in Andhra Pradesh according to the APSES 2025–26 figures?
x: Solar is the largest renewable-energy source in Andhra Pradesh, with an installed capacity of 5,614.52 MW.

s: What was the installed power capacity of Andhra Pradesh as of March 2022?
x: The PYQ key gives 25,726.89 MW (about 25.7 GW) as of March 2022. 27,392 MW is the 30 Nov 2024 figure, 21,297.03 MW is the Dec 2025 installed/contracted figure on a different basis, and 33,240 MW is AP's pumped-storage potential.

s: In which city is the 2,000 MW Simhadri power station located?
x: The Simhadri power station, with 2,000 MW (April 2025), is at Visakhapatnam.

s: What peak power demand did Andhra Pradesh record on 21 May 2026?
x: Peak demand reached 15,016 MW on 21 May 2026; 15,680 MW is the size of the expansion programme.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Maritime Policy 2024–29 aims to make the State India's leading what?
x: The AP Maritime Policy 2024–29 aims to make Andhra Pradesh India's leading maritime gateway.

s: The AP Maritime Policy 2024-29 targets what share of all-India port cargo by 2047?
x: The policy targets 20% of all-India port cargo by 2047 and at least one port in the world's top 20.

s: Which is the nodal body for non-major ports in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board is the nodal body for non-major ports in the State.

s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, where was the Government of India to examine establishing a major port?
x: The Act provided for examining a major port at Duggirajupatnam, a new railway zone and upgrades to the Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati airports.

s: Which is the only major port of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Visakhapatnam is AP's only major (Union) port; the others are non-major ports.

s: Which of the following pairs (port – district) is correctly matched?
x: Krishnapatnam is in Nellore; Mulapeta is in Srikakulam, Machilipatnam in Krishna and Gangavaram in Visakhapatnam.

s:
Consider the following statements about ports in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Gangavaram is a non-major private port operated by Adani.
2. Machilipatnam is a greenfield port on the landlord model.
3. Krishnapatnam is a major port.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Gangavaram (Adani) is non-major and private, and Machilipatnam is a greenfield landlord-model port; Krishnapatnam is a non-major private port, not a major port.

s: The AP Maritime Policy 2024-29 targets a port capacity of how much by 2047?
x: The policy targets 300 MTPA by 2047; the +145 MTPA figure is the addition targeted by 2030.

s: Which headland shelters the natural deep harbour of Visakhapatnam port?
x: Visakhapatnam port is a natural deep harbour sheltered by the Dolphin's Nose headland.

s: Iron ore from which mines is mainly exported through Visakhapatnam port?
x: Visakhapatnam port exports Bailadila iron ore, brought by the Kirandul-Kottavalasa line, mainly to Japan.

s: Which port of Andhra Pradesh is being developed on the BOOT model?
x: Vodarevu is on BOOT; Kakinada SEZ port became a commercial port via Swiss Challenge and Nakkapalli was declared a minor port.

s: What is the main focus of the wholly State-owned APIIC?
x: APIIC handles industrial infrastructure and land (parks, estates, SEZs, EMCs, land bank); industrial financing and promotion is APIDC's role.

s: APIIC can allot up to how many acres of land without Cabinet approval?
x: APIIC can allot up to 50 acres without Cabinet approval; after 1991 its role changed from manufacturer to facilitator.

s: In which year was APIDC, the body for industrial financing and promotion in Andhra Pradesh, set up?
x: APIDC was set up in 1960; APIIC came later, on 26 September 1973.

s: What is the size of the land bank of APIIC?
x: APIIC holds a land bank of 41,998 acres across 635 industrial clusters.

s: In which year was APIIC set up?
x: APIIC was set up on 26 September 1973; APIDC, the financing body, dates from 1960.

s: As of March 2016, which district of Andhra Pradesh had the most bank branches?
x: In March 2016 Guntur had the most bank branches, Anantapuram the most post offices and Visakhapatnam the most telephones.

s: When did Bhogapuram airport become operational?
x: Bhogapuram airport became operational on 1 August 2026; 1 June 2026 is when the SCoR zone became operational.

s: Which company is developing the Bhogapuram greenfield international airport in Vizianagaram district?
x: Bhogapuram is a greenfield international airport developed by GMR; it became operational on 1 August 2026.

s: Which of the following airports in Andhra Pradesh is a domestic airport?
x: Rajahmundry is a domestic airport; Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati are international airports.

s: Which airport was NOT among those the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 said would be upgraded?
x: APRA 2014 provided for upgrading Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati airports; Kadapa was not among them.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Industrial Corridor – Movement of goods, services and economic activity
NIMZ – Industrial development along with connectivity
Dedicated Freight Corridor – Dedicated railway freight infrastructure
Economic Corridor – Large areas with a world-class manufacturing ecosystem
x: A Dedicated Freight Corridor is dedicated railway freight infrastructure. An industrial corridor combines industry with connectivity, an economic corridor moves goods and services, and an NIMZ is a large manufacturing area.

s: Where is the headquarters of South Coast Railway, India's 18th railway zone?
x: SCoR is headquartered at Visakhapatnam, with Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam divisions; it became operational on 1 June 2026.

s: The creation of South Coast Railway was promised in which Schedule of the A.P. Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: South Coast Railway was promised in the Thirteenth Schedule and carved out of the South Central and East Coast Railways.

s: With which of the following does the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Policy 2024–29 give priority to industrial links?
o: Western DFC and Eastern DFC only
East Coast DFC and North–South DFC
x: The policy gives priority to links with the East Coast Dedicated Freight Corridor and the North–South Dedicated Freight Corridor.

s: The Raipur–Visakhapatnam greenfield expressway is associated with which programme?
x: The Raipur–Visakhapatnam greenfield expressway is described as a Bharatmala economic corridor.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with an industrial-corridor node in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Krishnapatnam is a node on CBIC. Kopparthy is a VCIC node and Orvakal is an HBIC (Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor) node.

s: Which of the following is NOT a division of South Coast Railway?
x: South Coast Railway's divisions are Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam; Rajahmundry is not one.

s: Which institution funds the Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC), part of the East Coast Economic Corridor?
x: VCIC is part of the East Coast Economic Corridor and is funded by the Asian Development Bank (ADB).

s: Which was Andhra Pradesh's first riverine (inland waterway) project?
x: The first riverine project is the Muktyala-Madipadu inland waterway on the Krishna.

s: From which date did South Coast Railway become operational?
x: South Coast Railway, India's 18th zone with HQ at Visakhapatnam, became operational on 1 June 2026.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated feature of the Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024?
o: Target of more than 160 GW of clean energy
x: The policy targets Net Zero by 2047, not by 2030. Its other stated features include over 160 GW of clean energy, ₹10 lakh crore investment and 7.5 lakh jobs.

s: The AP Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy, 2023 was folded into which policy?
x: The 2023 green hydrogen policy was absorbed into the AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024.

s: On which date was Andhra Pradesh's Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration, aiming to make the State the 'Green Hydrogen Capital', adopted at Amaravati?
x: The Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration was adopted at Amaravati on 19 July 2025.

s: By which year does the AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024 target Net Zero?
x: The policy targets Net Zero by 2047, not 2030, along with 160 GW+ clean energy.

s: Which is the nodal body for Andhra Pradesh's Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration?
x: SRM University is the nodal body of the Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration of 19 July 2025.

s: What clean energy capacity does the AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024 target?
x: The policy targets 160 GW+ clean energy, Rs 10 lakh crore investment and 7.5 lakh jobs.

s: What green hydrogen production target does the AP Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy, 2023 set for five years?
x: The 2023 policy targets 0.5 MTPA of green hydrogen or 2 MTPA of green ammonia in five years.

s: Which is the nodal agency of the AP Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy, 2023?
x: NREDCAP (New and Renewable Energy Development Corporation of AP) is the nodal agency of the policy.

s:
Consider the following statements about the AP Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy, 2023:
1. It targets 2 MTPA of green ammonia in five years.
2. It was later absorbed into the AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The policy targets 0.5 MTPA green hydrogen or 2 MTPA green ammonia, and it was absorbed into the Integrated Clean Energy Policy of June 2024.

s: Paradip, a hub under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, is in which State?
x: The Green Hydrogen hubs Paradip (Odisha), Kandla (Gujarat) and Tuticorin (Tamil Nadu) are all outside Andhra Pradesh.

s: Where was the Partnership Summit of 14-15 November 2025 held?
x: The Partnership Summit at Visakhapatnam (14-15 Nov 2025) drew proposals worth Rs 4.54 lakh crore.

s: Which one of the following is associated with solar power generation in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park is identified with solar power generation in Andhra Pradesh.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's identified pumped storage potential?
x: AP's pumped-storage potential is 29 sites totalling 33,240 MW, of which APGENCO has six approved PSPs (1,320 + 1,200 + 1,000 + 950 + 800 + 750 = about 6,020 MW). 15,680 MW is the generation expansion programme and 160 GW is the clean-energy policy target.

s: Who is taking up the 1,350 MW Upper Sileru Pumped Storage Project?
x: The APGENCO-NHPC JV (Sep 2024) covers five PSPs including Upper Sileru PSP of 1,350 MW. Tata Power is behind the Pathikonda-Kanekallu hybrid project, APGIC is an oil and gas company, and NTPC Green is not mentioned.

s: What is the capacity of Aravetipalli, the largest APGENCO-approved pumped storage project?
x: Aravetipalli is 1,320 MW; 1,350 MW is Upper Sileru, a project of the APGENCO-NHPC JV.

s: Where is the Ananthapuram-I Ultra Mega Solar Park located?
x: Ananthapuram-I solar park (about 1,500 MW) is at NP Kunta; Kurnool's is at Panyam and Ananthapuram-II at Talaricheruvu.

s: Which company is setting up the 800 MW solar-wind hybrid project at Pathikonda and Kanekallu?
x: Tata Power is setting up an 800 MW hybrid (solar plus wind) project at Pathikonda and Kanekallu at Rs 5,750 crore.

s: In what ratio is the equity of APGIC held by APIIC and APGENCO?
x: APGIC is 51% APIIC and 49% APGENCO; it was set up on 2 September 2009 and is a partner in a KG exploration consortium.

s: Where is the BPCL refinery-cum-petrochemical complex in Andhra Pradesh coming up?
x: BPCL's refinery-cum-petrochemical complex (about 9 MTPA, with an ethylene cracker) is at Ramayapatnam in Nellore.

s: In which year was APGIC, the APIIC-APGENCO gas venture, set up?
x: APGIC was set up on 2 September 2009 with APIIC holding 51% and APGENCO 49%.

s: Where is the ONGC mini-refinery in Andhra Pradesh located?
x: ONGC runs a mini-refinery at Tatipaka (East Godavari) on KG basin crude; the main refinery is HPCL Visakhapatnam.

s: The East-West gas pipeline laid by Reliance in 2009 runs from Kakinada to which place?
x: The East-West pipeline carries KG basin gas from Kakinada to Bharuch in Gujarat (Reliance, 2009).

s: Which company runs the main oil refinery of Andhra Pradesh at Visakhapatnam?
x: The main refinery is HPCL Visakhapatnam; ONGC runs only a mini-refinery at Tatipaka and BPCL's complex is coming up at Ramayapatnam.

s: For what is the Kakinada-Konaseema region of Andhra Pradesh known?
x: The Kakinada-Konaseema region is AP's oil and gas hub, associated with the KG basin.

s: The AP Retail Trade Policy 2015-20 targeted how many jobs by 2020?
x: The policy targeted Rs 5,000 crore investment and 20,000 jobs by 2020.

s: What was the investment target of the AP Retail Trade Policy 2015-20?
x: The Retail Trade Policy 2015-20 aimed at Rs 5,000 crore investment and 20,000 jobs by 2020.

s:
Consider the following statements about the AP Retail Trade Policy 2015-20:
1. It aimed to make Andhra Pradesh a preferred retail destination.
2. It sought to promote e-commerce.
3. It aimed to train 5 lakh youth in five years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The policy aimed to make AP a preferred retail destination and to promote e-commerce; its training target was 1 lakh youth in five years, not 5 lakh.

s: The AP Tourism Policy 2024-29 is aligned with which vision?
x: The policy is aligned with Swarna Andhra @2047, not Viksit Bharat @2047.

s: What status has the AP Tourism Policy 2024-29 given to tourism and hospitality?
o: Industry status only for Mega projects
Industry status only for heritage hotels
x: Tourism and hospitality got industry status across all segments, with fiscal, recurring, special and non-fiscal incentives and tailor-made packages for Mega and Ultra Mega projects.

s: Among India's top how many tourist destinations does the AP Tourism Policy 2024-29 aim to place Andhra Pradesh?
x: The policy targets a top-three rank, with tourism above 20% of State GVA and 20% of the workforce.

s: Budget hotels were promoted in Andhra Pradesh mainly with which objective?
o: To restrict private investment in tourism
To provide accommodation exclusively to government employees
x: Budget hotels were promoted mainly to attract tourists by expanding affordable accommodation facilities.

s: At which event was Swarna Andhra Tourism Vision 2047 unveiled?
x: The vision was unveiled at the FAITH conclave; AP separately won the Best Tourism Promotion State award at GTM 2026.

s: Above what share of the State GVA does the AP Tourism Policy 2024-29 target for tourism?
x: The policy targets tourism above 20% of State GVA and 20% of the workforce.

s: At which event did Andhra Pradesh win 'Best Tourism Promotion State'?
x: AP won Best Tourism Promotion State at GTM 2026; the Swarna Andhra Tourism Vision 2047 was launched at the FAITH conclave.

s: What were the tourist arrivals in Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26?
x: Tourist arrivals in AP were 36.42 crore in 2025-26.

s: Which country was the most visited in the world in 2024?
x: France was the most visited country in 2024, followed by Spain and the USA.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank among States in domestic tourist visits in 2024?
x: As per Ministry of Tourism data for 2024, Andhra Pradesh (about 29 crore visits) was 4th after Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.

s: Which body is the fully State-owned operational arm of tourism in Andhra Pradesh, running Haritha hotels and the Srisailam ropeway?
x: APTDC is the State-owned operational arm running Haritha hotels, boating, sound-and-light shows and the Srisailam ropeway; PRASHAD is a Union Ministry of Tourism scheme.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: SASCI — Gandikota Fort and Gorge — ₹25.32 crore
x: The PRASHAD project at Annavaram temple has a cost of ₹25.32 crore. The other options incorrectly interchange schemes, projects or costs.

s: CBDD projects under Swadesh Darshan 2.0 in Andhra Pradesh include which of the following?
x: The CBDD projects are Ahobilam, described as spiritual, and Nagarjunasagar, described as heritage and adventure. Each has a cost of ₹25 crore.

s: How many projects were sanctioned nationally under Swadesh Darshan 2.0?
x: Swadesh Darshan 2.0 had 52 projects nationally, while PRASHAD had 54.

s: Which pair of Andhra Pradesh tourism projects has been taken up under SASCI (Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment)?
o: Gandikota Fort and Gorge, and Havelock Bridge with Pushkar ghat at Rajahmundry
x: SASCI funds Gandikota Fort and Gorge (Rs 77.91 crore) and Havelock Bridge + Pushkar ghat, Rajahmundry (Rs 94.44 crore). Borra Caves is under Swadesh Darshan 2.0 and Simhachalam/Annavaram under PRASHAD; Ahobilam and Nagarjunasagar are CBDD projects.

s: What is the full form of CBDD, a sub-scheme of Swadesh Darshan 2.0?
x: CBDD is Challenge Based Destination Development, a sub-scheme of Swadesh Darshan 2.0; SASCI is Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Swadesh Darshan 1.0 (thematic circuits) had 76 projects sanctioned, of which 75 were completed.

s: How many projects have been sanctioned nationally under the PRASHAD scheme?
x: PRASHAD has 54 projects; 52 is the Swadesh Darshan 2.0 count.

s: Under which scheme is the Simhachalam temple project in Andhra Pradesh taken up?
x: Simhachalam temple (Rs 54.04 crore) is a PRASHAD project, as is Annavaram.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh project has been sanctioned under Swadesh Darshan 2.0?
x: Borra Caves at Araku (Rs 29.87 crore) is under Swadesh Darshan 2.0; Simhachalam and Annavaram are PRASHAD, Gandikota is SASCI.

s: In which year was the Swadesh Darshan scheme launched?
x: Swadesh Darshan 1.0 was launched in January 2015 for thematic circuits.

s: In which year was the India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC) set up?
x: ITDC was set up in October 1966 to develop tourism and hotels nationally.

s: Which Union Ministry runs the PRASHAD scheme?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
x: PRASHAD, which funds the Simhachalam and Annavaram temple projects in AP, is a Union Ministry of Tourism scheme.

s: Andhra Pradesh is described as the birthplace of which form of Buddhism?
x: AP is described as the birthplace of Mahayana Buddhism and has about 40 Buddhist monuments.

s: Which of the following is NOT included among the Buddhist circuit sites identified in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The listed Buddhist sites include Amaravati, Thotlakonda, Bavikonda, Bojjannakonda, Sankaram, Salihundam and Ghantasala. Srisailam is not included in this Buddhist-site list.

s: Which beach in Andhra Pradesh has received Blue Flag recognition?
x: Rushikonda Beach has received Blue Flag recognition.

s: On which State's policy is Andhra Pradesh's proposed beach-shack policy modelled?
x: The beach-shack policy is modelled on Goa's; AP has also sought a shift of Vizag Beach Road from CRZ-3 to CRZ-2.

s: What kind of coach runs on the Visakhapatnam-Araku train?
x: The Visakhapatnam-Araku train has a glass-roofed Vistadome coach for tourists.

s: Where are the multimodal logistics parks identified in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Visakhapatnam and Ananthapur are the identified multimodal logistics park sites in AP.

s: In LEADS 2024, Andhra Pradesh was placed in which category?
x: AP slipped from Achiever (2022) to Fast Mover in LEADS 2024.

s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh in the LEADS ranking:
1. It was an Achiever in 2022.
2. It remained an Achiever in 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: AP was an Achiever in LEADS 2022 but slipped to Fast Mover in 2024.

s: Where is the Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone (AMTZ), the medical-device hub, located?
x: AMTZ is at Visakhapatnam; Amaravati has the 'Eye Tourism' zone, AIIMS Mangalagiri anchors eSanjeevani and IITTM Nellore trains hospitality staff.

s: With which place is the approved 'Eye Tourism' medical zone associated?
x: An Eye Tourism medical zone was approved in Amaravati.

s: Which of the following institutions is associated with the proposed education hub at Amaravati?
x: VIT, SRM and Amrita are associated with Amaravati; IIT Tirupati is not listed among the institutions hosted there.

s: How many regional medical hubs for medical tourism did the Union Budget 2026-27 propose?
x: The Union Budget 2026-27 proposed five regional medical hubs, along with five university townships in industrial corridors.

s: Which institution in Andhra Pradesh leads eSanjeevani?
x: AIIMS Mangalagiri leads eSanjeevani; AMTZ is a medical-device hub and IITTM Nellore trains hospitality staff.

s: Which institution at Nellore trains hospitality staff?
x: The Indian Institute of Tourism and Travel Management (IITTM) at Nellore trains hospitality staff.

s: How many university townships in industrial corridors did the Union Budget 2026-27 propose?
x: The Union Budget 2026-27 proposed five university townships in industrial corridors, along with five regional medical hubs.
